event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: A thorough review of the provided Form 10-K excerpt reveals no explicit or even indirect references to COVID-19-related risks such as supply-chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote-work transitions, or shifts in consumer demand. The text merely points the reader to other sections of the 2022 Annual Report without reproducing any substantive risk disclosure. Because the assignment confines the analysis to the supplied “DOCUMENT TEXT,” there is no content tying USB’s risk profile to the COVID-19 pandemic. Under the Time Decay Principle, an event that began in March 2020 would normally allow for a high severity score (it is within three years of the February 2023 filing). However, in the absence of any pertinent language, the risk evidence score must be zero.
